# penult

From an idea to a publication draft: the penultimate step, where the essay exists, is illustrated, sounds like its author, and waits for them to say go.

```bash
pip install penult
```

The seed is a GitHub issue. An agent, with the `penult` skill, turns it into an essay posted as a comment on that issue for the author to review, and, once the author approves, into an **unpublished** Substack or Medium draft through [article](https://github.com/thorwhalen/article). penult never publishes to a platform; the draft is as public as the issue it is posted on.

```bash
penult start https://github.com/you/essays/issues/30     # workspace docs/<slug>/ in the repo: seed.md, brief.md, state
penult status docs/<slug>                                 # stage, files, what comes next
penult check docs/<slug>                                  # ductus + penlike over essay.md; the report goes under ~/.local/share/penult, not the repo
penult image-search "a 1995 modem" --folder docs/<slug>   # credited stock / public-domain candidates
penult image-generate "<prompt>" --name hero --folder docs/<slug>   # at most 2 automatically; prompts past that are kept for you
penult layout docs/<slug> --apply                         # size class per image (a square hero becomes an inset), into the front matter
penult render docs/<slug> && penult post docs/<slug>      # the essay as an issue comment, images by raw URL
penult approve docs/<slug> --note "good to go"            # the author's words; this gates publishing
penult publish docs/<slug>                                # an unpublished Substack draft; you press Publish
```

## What penult holds, and what the agent does

The thinking is the agent’s: the research that checks every claim and finds the critiques, the draft, the passes that make it sound like the author. The `penult` skill lays that out and names the skills that own each step (`do-research`, `penlike` and its author-choice guide, `deslop`, `ductus`, `illustration`).

penult holds what should not be improvised twice:

- **the workspace**: `docs/<slug>/` next to the issue, with the seed as fetched, the brief (angle, audience, voice, platform, image budget, assumptions), the research notes, `essay.md`, `images.md` with every candidate, prompt and credit, `img/`, and a state file;
- **the thin-seed gate**: a seed with no thesis or too few words is reported, and the agent asks the author before researching;
- **the image budget**: paid generation capped per essay (two by default); every prompt is kept so the author can try the rest by hand;
- **the layout rules**: each image has a size class (`inset`, `normal`, `large`, `full`) in `essay.md`’s front matter, suggested from its pixels by `penult layout` (a square or portrait image, or a non-landscape hero, is an inset; landscape, diagrams and charts take the column) and honoured both in the comment (`<img width>`) and on Substack (python-substack’s image marker); the research behind the rules is in `misc/docs/research/`;
- **the review loop**: the essay rendered for a GitHub comment (title, subtitle, images turned into raw URLs and sized, captions drawn small under them), posted and updated in place, refusing while an image is not pushed;
- **the approval gate**: `publish` runs only after `approve`, of the exact text that was posted, and only makes a draft; images in the comment are pinned to the pushed commit so the links outlive the branch.

## Your preferences stay private

Voices, platform, image budget, where the `article` credentials file is: `penult prefs` shows them, `penult prefs-set <key> <value>` changes one. They live under `~/.local/share/penult` (set `PENULT_DATA_DIR` to move it), never in a project folder. Credentials are never read by penult itself; `publish` hands the path of the credentials file to `article`.

| Preference             | Default                                                               | Meaning                                                                           |
|------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `voice_models`         | `["me"]`                                                              | the penlike models the style pass writes with; the first is the base voice        |
| `voice_register`       | `essay`                                                               | the penlike register to measure against                                           |
| `audience`             | non-technical readers, or software engineers, managers and scientists | narrowed per essay in the brief                                                   |
| `platform`             | `substack`                                                            | where `publish` sends the approved essay (`substack` or `medium`)                 |
| `max_generated_images` | `2`                                                                   | paid images generated automatically per essay                                     |
| `min_image_prompts`    | `5`                                                                   | prompts the agent writes into `images.md`                                         |
| `inset_width`          | `400`                                                                 | how wide an `inset` image is drawn, in CSS pixels, in the comment and on Substack |
| `article_env_file`     | `~/.config/article/.env`                                              | the `article` credentials file                                                    |
| `article_state_path`   | `~/.local/share/article/pipeline_state.json`                          | the `article` state file                                                          |
| `workspace`            | `docs/{slug}`                                                         | where a workspace goes in the issue’s repository                                  |
| `research_depth`       | `deep`                                                                | the `do-research` depth                                                           |

## From Python

Every command is a function in `penult.tools`, taking and returning JSON-ready values. The in-memory store (`files=`), the issue fetcher (`fetch=`), the command runner (`runner=`), the image searcher and generator (`searcher=`, `generator=`) are keyword arguments, which is how the tests run without a network:

```python
import penult
started = penult.start("https://github.com/you/essays/issues/30", into="docs/my-essay")
penult.image_generate("a woodcut of a modem", name="hero", folder="docs/my-essay")
penult.render("docs/my-essay"); penult.post("docs/my-essay")
```

## Install the skill

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/penult penult --agent claude-code   # needs a GitHub CLI with `gh skill`
```

Or copy (or symlink) `penult/data/skills/penult/` into your agent’s skills folder; it ships with the package. Extras: `pip install 'penult[publish]'` for the Substack step, `'penult[images]'` for search and generation, `'penult[style]'` for the checks.

## Related

- [article](https://github.com/thorwhalen/article): Markdown to an unpublished Substack draft, and syndication with canonical URLs. penult’s publishing step.
- [penlike](https://github.com/thorwhalen/penlike): how an author writes, and the author-choice guide (`penlike guide`).
- [ductus](https://github.com/thorwhalen/ductus): which passages read as machine-written, and why.
- [illustration](https://github.com/thorwhalen/illustration): existing images with licence and attribution.

# _autosummary/penult.figures.html.md

# penult.figures

Illustration layout: how big each image is drawn, and where, on every renderer.

The rules come from `misc/docs/research/2026-11-06-illustration-layout-for-essays.md`
(sourced where it could be, judgment where it says so). The short version:

- An image has a **size class**: `inset` (about half the column, centred), `normal`
  (the column, the default), `large` (wider than the column; Substack renders it on
  the web only) or `full` (edge to edge; opt-in, for an image that *is* the content).
  The vocabulary mirrors what Substack, Medium and the Guardian’s renderer already have.
- The **hero** (the first image, under the title) is landscape at column width, or an
  inset. A square or portrait image at column width is drawn taller than a laptop
  screen, which is the complaint this module exists to answer.
- A body image that is square or portrait is an inset; a landscape one, a diagram or a
  chart is `normal`. Few images: after the hero, at most one per 500-1000 words.
- Captions are one line, not italic (the platforms draw them small, centred, upright).

The class lives in the essay’s front matter, out of the Markdown that goes to the
publisher:

```default
images:
  img/hero.png: inset
```

A GitHub comment honours it as `<img width>`; python-substack honours it through its
own `<!-- python-substack-image:v1 ... -->` marker, which [`substack_markdown()`](_autosummary/penult.figures.html.md#penult.figures.substack_markdown)
writes after each sized image. Neither `{width=...}` nor `<img>` may go to
python-substack (the first turns the image into its alt text, the second drops it).

```pycon
>>> sizes_from_fields({"images": {"img/a.png": "inset"}})
{'img/a.png': 'inset'}
>>> suggest_size(1024, 1024, hero=True)
('inset', 'square hero: at column width it is taller than a laptop screen')
>>> suggest_size(1456, 819, hero=True)
('normal', 'landscape hero (16:9) fits the column')
```

|-----------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`COLUMN_WIDTH`](_autosummary/penult.figures.html.md#penult.figures.COLUMN_WIDTH)   | Substack's post column, in CSS pixels (measured; the research report, section 2).                                                      |
| [`INSET_WIDTH`](_autosummary/penult.figures.html.md#penult.figures.INSET_WIDTH)    | a little over half the column, inside the Guardian's "supporting" range and Wikipedia's 400 px ceiling.                                |
| [`GITHUB_ATTRS`](_autosummary/penult.figures.html.md#penult.figures.GITHUB_ATTRS)   | `<img>` attributes per class for a GitHub comment (the comment is already about the column's width, so only `inset` narrows anything). |
| [`SUBSTACK_ATTRS`](_autosummary/penult.figures.html.md#penult.figures.SUBSTACK_ATTRS) | `image2` attributes per class for python-substack.                                                                                     |

### penult.figures.SIZES *= ('inset', 'normal', 'large', 'full')*

### penult.figures.SUBSTACK_ATTRS *: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]]* *= {'full': {'fullscreen': True}, 'inset': {'resizeWidth': 400}, 'large': {'imageSize': 'large'}, 'normal': {}}*

`image2` attributes per class for python-substack. `resizeWidth` is what the
editor’s own resize handle writes. `large` and `full` are the values the
stylesheet’s `sizing-large` / `sizing-fullscreen` classes imply; a draft sized
in the editor and read back would confirm them (the report’s open item).

### penult.figures.substack_markdown(markdown, sizes=None, , inset_width=400)

The essay with a python-substack image marker after each image whose class says so.

The marker is an HTML comment python-substack merges into the `image2` node;
GitHub and every Markdown viewer hide it. Front matter and the image lines are
unchanged, so `article`’s checks apply as before.

```pycon
>>> out = substack_markdown('---\ntitle: T\nimages:\n  img/a.png: inset\n---\n# T\n\n![a](img/a.png "c")\n')
>>> out.splitlines()[-1].startswith("<!-- python-substack-image:v1 ")
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

# _autosummary/penult.github.html.md

# penult.github

GitHub, through the `gh` and `git` commands: read an issue, post or edit a comment, find raw URLs.

Every function takes a `runner` (the shape of [`subprocess.run()`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/subprocess.html#subprocess.run)) so tests
run without a network and another transport can be dropped in. The default needs
an authenticated `gh`.

```pycon
>>> parse_issue_url("https://github.com/octo/essays/issues/30")
('octo', 'essays', 30)
```

### Functions

| [`edit_comment`](_autosummary/penult.github.html.md#penult.github.edit_comment)(comment_url, body_file, \*[, runner])   | Replace an existing comment's body (`comment_url` ends in `#issuecomment-<id>`).        |
|-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`fetch_issue`](_autosummary/penult.github.html.md#penult.github.fetch_issue)(url, \*[, runner])                       | The issue's title, body, labels and comments, as one JSON-ready dict.                   |
| [`parse_issue_url`](_autosummary/penult.github.html.md#penult.github.parse_issue_url)(url)                                 | `(owner, repo, number)` from an issue URL, or an error that shows the shape.            |
| [`post_comment`](_autosummary/penult.github.html.md#penult.github.post_comment)(url, body_file, \*[, runner])           | Post a file's content as a comment on the issue; returns the comment's URL.             |
| [`raw_url_base`](_autosummary/penult.github.html.md#penult.github.raw_url_base)(checkout, folder)                       | The `raw.githubusercontent.com` prefix for files in `folder` at the checkout's commit.  |
| [`repo_of_checkout`](_autosummary/penult.github.html.md#penult.github.repo_of_checkout)(path, \*[, runner])                 | The checkout holding `path`: its root, GitHub owner/repo, branch and commit, or `None`. |
| [`unpushed`](_autosummary/penult.github.html.md#penult.github.unpushed)(checkout, paths, \*[, runner])              | Which of `paths` are not yet committed and pushed to the branch's upstream.             |

### penult.github.edit_comment(comment_url, body_file, \*, runner=<function run>)

Replace an existing comment’s body (`comment_url` ends in `#issuecomment-<id>`).

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### penult.github.fetch_issue(url, \*, runner=<function run>)

The issue’s title, body, labels and comments, as one JSON-ready dict.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

### penult.github.parse_issue_url(url)

`(owner, repo, number)` from an issue URL, or an error that shows the shape.

* **Return type:**
  [`tuple`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#tuple)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)]

### penult.github.post_comment(url, body_file, \*, runner=<function run>)

Post a file’s content as a comment on the issue; returns the comment’s URL.

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### penult.github.raw_url_base(checkout, folder)

The `raw.githubusercontent.com` prefix for files in `folder` at the checkout’s commit.

The commit, not the branch, so the links keep working after the branch is
merged and deleted.

```pycon
>>> raw_url_base({"root": "/r", "owner": "o", "repo": "e", "branch": "main", "sha": "abc123"}, Path("/r/docs/an essay"))
'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/o/e/abc123/docs/an%20essay/'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### penult.github.repo_of_checkout(path, \*, runner=<function run>)

The checkout holding `path`: its root, GitHub owner/repo, branch and commit, or `None`.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)] | [`None`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/constants.html#None)

### penult.github.unpushed(checkout, paths, \*, runner=<function run>)

Which of `paths` are not yet committed and pushed to the branch’s upstream.

A raw URL only works for a file that is on GitHub, so `post` refuses while any
image it references is in this list. Paths are compared in git’s own form
(forward slashes, unescaped thanks to `-z`).

* **Return type:**
  [`list`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#list)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)]


# _autosummary/penult.html.md

# penult

penult: from an idea to a publication draft, posted where its author can review it.

The seed is a GitHub issue. penult fetches it into a workspace next to it, holds the
brief, the research notes, the essay, the images and their credits, checks the draft
with ductus and penlike, renders it as an issue comment, and, once the author says
so, hands it to `article` for an unpublished Substack or Medium draft. The
thinking in between (research, drafting, the style passes) is an agent’s, laid out
in the `penult` skill; the verbs here keep every step from being improvised twice.

```pycon
>>> import penult
>>> penult.prefs(files={})["preferences"]["platform"]
'substack'
```

### Functions

| [`approve`](_autosummary/penult.html.md#penult.approve)([folder, by, note])                        | Record that the person is happy with the posted draft, as it stands now; this lets `publish` run.   |
|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`check`](_autosummary/penult.html.md#penult.check)([folder, like, style, out, data_dir, ...])   | Read the essay with ductus and penlike, and write what they found to a private check file.          |
| [`data_dir`](_autosummary/penult.html.md#penult.data_dir)([data_dir])                               | The data root: the argument, else `$PENULT_DATA_DIR`, else the user data folder.                    |
| [`image_add`](_autosummary/penult.html.md#penult.image_add)(source, \*, name, credit[, folder, ...]) | Add an image (a URL or a local file) to img/ with its credit; `--prompt` if a person generated it.  |
| [`image_generate`](_autosummary/penult.html.md#penult.image_generate)(prompt, \*, name[, folder, ...])    | Generate one image from `prompt` into img/, within the `max_generated_images` budget.               |
| [`image_search`](_autosummary/penult.html.md#penult.image_search)(query, \*[, folder, n, searcher])     | Find existing stock, Creative-Commons or public-domain images for `query`, credited.                |
| [`layout`](_autosummary/penult.html.md#penult.layout)([folder, apply])                            | Each image's size class against the layout rules; `--apply` writes the suggestions.                 |
| [`mark`](_autosummary/penult.html.md#penult.mark)([folder])                                     | Record that the workspace reached `stage` (researched, drafted, styled, illustrated).               |

### penult.approve(folder=None, , by='the user', note='')

Record that the person is happy with the posted draft, as it stands now; this lets `publish` run.

Only set it when the person said so, in their words; quote them in `--note`. The
approval is of this text: if essay.md changes afterwards, `publish` refuses until
the person approves again.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### penult.check(folder=None, \*, like=None, style=None, out=None, data_dir=None, files=None, runner=<function run>)

Read the essay with ductus and penlike, and write what they found to a private check file.

ductus marks the segments that read machine-made (lean toward +1, with the
evidence strength); penlike measures the draft against each voice model in
`like` (the `voice_models` preference by default). The report quotes figures
from the author’s private style models, so it goes under the data root
(`work/<slug>/check.md`), not into the workspace, unless `out` says where.
The agent’s own reading comes on top of this; neither tool sees bland prose that
carries no tell.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### penult.image_search(query, , folder=None, n=8, searcher=None)

Find existing stock, Creative-Commons or public-domain images for `query`, credited.

Candidates are recorded in images.md. Download the one you use with
`image-add <url> --name <file> --credit "<the credit line shown>"`.

### penult.layout(folder=None, , apply=False)

Each image’s size class against the layout rules; `--apply` writes the suggestions.

The rules (`penult.figures`, from the layout research in `misc/docs/research/`):
the hero is landscape at column width or an inset; a square or portrait body image
is an inset; a landscape one, a diagram or a chart takes the column; after the hero,
about one image per 500 words at most. The class goes in essay.md’s `images:`
front matter, which `render` honours as `<img width>` and `publish` as
python-substack’s image marker. `--apply` sets every unset image’s class to the
suggestion (a class set by hand is kept; to change one, edit the front matter).

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### penult.publish(folder=None, \*, platform=None, dry_run=False, data_dir=None, files=None, runner=<function run>, publisher=None)

Hand the approved essay to the publisher for an **unpublished** draft on the platform.

The default publisher is the `article` package (Substack draft, or Medium’s
import step); the draft’s editor link comes back and the person publishes by
hand. Refuses before `penult approve`, and after any change to essay.md since
the approval, unless `--dry-run` (which converts and checks, sending nothing).

  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

Write comment.md: the essay as a GitHub comment, relative images turned into raw URLs.

`raw_base` is worked out from the checkout (owner, repo, commit, folder) when
not given; pinning the commit keeps the links alive after the branch is merged.
The comment ends with a footer naming the seed and the research folder.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

### penult.start(seed, \*, into=None, force=False, data_dir=None, files=None, fetch=None, runner=<function run>)

Fetch the seed (a GitHub issue URL) and make the workspace: seed, brief, state.

The workspace goes `into` the folder given, else to the `workspace` preference
(`docs/<slug>` by default) inside the checkout of the issue’s own repository
that holds the current directory. A thin seed (few words, no thesis) is reported
so the agent asks the user before researching. `--force` refetches the seed into
an existing workspace; the brief and the stage are kept.

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)

# _autosummary/penult.images.html.md

# penult.images

Images for the essay: find existing ones, generate a few, and keep the ledger.

Three sources, one ledger (`images.md` in the workspace, mirrored in the state):

- **search**: existing stock, Creative-Commons and public-domain images through the
  `illustration` package, which carries licence and attribution with each hit;
- **generate**: a paid image from a prompt through `aix.image.generate_image`,
  capped by the person’s `max_generated_images` so that an off prompt does not
  cost much; every prompt is kept in the ledger whether or not it was run;
- **add**: an image the person made or found themselves, with its credit.

The searcher and the generator are seams: any callable of the same shape works, and
tests pass fakes.

```pycon
>>> credit_line({"title": "Harbour", "author": "A. Painter", "license": "cc-by", "source": "openverse"})
'Harbour, by A. Painter (cc-by, via openverse)'
```

|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`credit_line`](_autosummary/penult.images.html.md#penult.images.credit_line)(record)                              | A one-line credit from a record: the attribution if the source gave one, else built. |
| [`default_generator`](_autosummary/penult.images.html.md#penult.images.default_generator)(prompt, \*, path, \*\*options) | Generate one image with `aix` (DALL-E 3 and other litellm providers) and save it.    |
| [`default_searcher`](_autosummary/penult.images.html.md#penult.images.default_searcher)(query, \*[, n])                 | The `illustration` package's unified search (Openverse by default, no key needed).   |
| [`generate_image`](_autosummary/penult.images.html.md#penult.images.generate_image)(ws, prompt, \*, name, ...[, ...]) | Generate one image from `prompt` into `img/`, within the budget.                     |
| [`search_images`](_autosummary/penult.images.html.md#penult.images.search_images)(ws, query, \*[, n, searcher])      | Find existing images for `query` and record the candidates in the ledger.            |

# _autosummary/penult.store.html.md

# penult.store

Where penult’s private data lives, and the preferences read from it.

Everything a person tells penult about how they want their drafts made is private:
which voices, which platform, how many paid images, where their publishing
credentials are. None of it belongs in a repository. It lives under the data root:

```default
<data root>/config/preferences.json
```

The data root is the `data_dir` argument, else `$PENULT_DATA_DIR`, else
`~/.local/share/penult` (`$XDG_DATA_HOME` and `%LOCALAPPDATA%` are honoured).

Code reaches the files through a `MutableMapping` of relative path to text, so the
local folder can be swapped for any other store (or a plain dict in tests) without
touching the rest:

```pycon
>>> prefs = preferences(files={})
>>> prefs["max_generated_images"], prefs["platform"]
(2, 'substack')
>>> files = {}
>>> set_preference("platform", "medium", files=files)["platform"]
'medium'
>>> preferences(files=files)["platform"]
'medium'
```

### Module Attributes

| [`DEFAULT_PREFERENCES`](_autosummary/penult.store.html.md#penult.store.DEFAULT_PREFERENCES)   | The preferences every verb falls back to.   |
|------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------|

### Functions

|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`preferences`](_autosummary/penult.store.html.md#penult.store.preferences)(\*[, data_dir, files])                | The preferences: the defaults, overlaid with what the person wrote.                   |
| [`set_preference`](_autosummary/penult.store.html.md#penult.store.set_preference)(key, value, \*[, data_dir, files]) | Set one preference and return the whole set.                                          |
| [`text_files`](_autosummary/penult.store.html.md#penult.store.text_files)(root)                                  | A `dol` files store under `root`: `/`-separated keys, UTF-8 text values.              |
| [`write_preferences`](_autosummary/penult.store.html.md#penult.store.write_preferences)(values, \*[, data_dir, files])  | Replace the saved preferences (only the keys that differ from the defaults are kept). |

### penult.store.DEFAULT_PREFERENCES *: [dict](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[str](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [Any](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]* *= {'article_env_file': '~/.config/article/.env', 'article_state_path': '~/.local/share/article/pipeline_state.json', 'audience': 'non-technical readers, or software engineers, managers and scientists', 'inset_width': 400, 'max_generated_images': 2, 'min_image_prompts': 5, 'platform': 'substack', 'research_depth': 'deep', 'voice_models': ['me'], 'voice_register': 'essay', 'workspace': 'docs/{slug}'}*

The preferences every verb falls back to. A person changes them with
`penult prefs-set`; an agent changes them only when the person said so.

# _autosummary/penult.tools.html.md

# penult.tools

The verbs: plain functions, JSON-ready in and out, the one list every surface is built from.

An agent drives an essay from a seed to a reviewed draft with these, in this order:

```default
start      fetch the seed (a GitHub issue), make the workspace, say whether it is thin
status     where the workspace stands and what comes next
mark       record a stage reached by the agent's own work (researched, drafted, ...)
check      ductus and penlike over the essay: what still reads machine-made or off-voice
image-search / image-generate / image-add   images, within the budget, all credited
render     the essay as an issue comment, images as raw URLs pinned to the commit
post       post (or update) that comment on the issue
approve    record that the person is happy with the posted draft, as it was then
publish    hand the approved essay to ``article`` for an unpublished platform draft
prefs / prefs-set   the private preferences
```

The thinking (research, drafting, the style passes) is the agent’s and is laid out
in the `penult` skill; these verbs hold the state, the files, the budget and the
hand-offs so that no step is improvised twice. Nothing here prints or exits: the
command line and any other surface wrap [`TOOLS`](_autosummary/penult.tools.html.md#penult.tools.TOOLS).

### Module Attributes

| [`HIDDEN_PARAMETERS`](_autosummary/penult.tools.html.md#penult.tools.HIDDEN_PARAMETERS)   | the in-memory store and the injected callables are for Python callers and tests.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`TOOLS`](_autosummary/penult.tools.html.md#penult.tools.TOOLS)               | The one list every surface is built from.                                          |

### Functions

| [`without`](_autosummary/penult.tools.html.md#penult.tools.without)(func[, hidden])   | The same verb with `hidden` parameters removed from its signature.   |
|----------------------------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------|

### penult.tools.HIDDEN_PARAMETERS *= ('files', 'fetch', 'runner', 'searcher', 'generator', 'publisher')*

the in-memory store and
the injected callables are for Python callers and tests.

* **Type:**
  Parameters a surface built from these signatures leaves out

### penult.tools.TOOLS *= [<function start>, <function status>, <function mark>, <function check>, <function image_search>, <function image_generate>, <function image_add>, <function layout>, <function render>, <function post>, <function approve>, <function publish>, <function prefs>, <function prefs_set>]*

The one list every surface is built from. Never write a second one.

### penult.tools.without(func, hidden=('files', 'fetch', 'runner', 'searcher', 'generator', 'publisher'))

The same verb with `hidden` parameters removed from its signature.

```pycon
>>> "files" in inspect.signature(without(prefs)).parameters
False
```

* **Return type:**
  [`Callable`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Callable)


# _autosummary/penult.workspace.html.md

# penult.workspace

One essay’s workspace: its files, its state, and the seed and brief written into it.

A workspace is a folder, by default `docs/<slug>/` inside the issue’s repository,
so that the research notes, the essay and its images are versioned next to the
issue they came from and found by whoever indexes that repository’s docs:

```default
<workspace>/
    penult.json      state: the issue, the stage, the images, the comment, the draft
    seed.md          the issue as fetched: title, body, comments
    brief.md         angle, audience, voice, platform, image budget, assumptions
    research/        the research notes (Vancouver references), one file per theme
    essay.md         the draft, with front matter for title and subtitle
    images.md        every image candidate and prompt, with credit and licence
    img/             the images the essay uses
    comment.md       the essay rendered for an issue comment
```

The style check (`penult check`) is written under the private data root, not
here: it quotes figures from the author’s private style models.

```pycon
>>> ws = Workspace("/tmp/x/docs/an-essay")
>>> ws.essay.name, ws.state_file.name
('essay.md', 'penult.json')
```

### Functions

| [`is_thin`](_autosummary/penult.workspace.html.md#penult.workspace.is_thin)(issue, \*[, threshold])   | Whether the seed is too thin to research and draft from without asking.   |

### penult.workspace.is_thin(issue, , threshold=250)

Whether the seed is too thin to research and draft from without asking.

A thin seed is one with fewer than `threshold` words in title, body and
comments together. The result says why, so the agent can quote it in the
questions it sends.

```pycon
>>> is_thin({"title": "An idea", "body": "Agents read specs.", "comments": []})["thin"]
True
```

* **Return type:**
  [`dict`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#dict)[[`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str), [`Any`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/typing.html#typing.Any)]

### penult.workspace.slug_of(title, , max_length=60)

A folder-safe slug from a title, cut at a word boundary.

```pycon

'ai-and-the-accretion-trap-why-experts-underestimate-broken'
```

* **Return type:**
  [`str`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/stdtypes.html#str)

### penult.workspace.word_count(text)

How many whitespace-separated words a text has.

```pycon
>>> word_count("one two  three\nfour")
4
```

* **Return type:**
  [`int`](https://docs.python.org/3/builtins/functions.html#int)

# ai-agents.html.md

<!-- generated by epythet -->

# For AI agents

`penult` ships artifacts for coding agents alongside its code. This page lists
them, says where each lives in the repository, and points at the
machine-readable copies of this documentation.

## Skills

Skills are folders holding a `SKILL.md` (the [Agent Skills](https://agentskills.io) format): a description that tells an agent when to use it and a body with the procedure. Install one into your agent with `gh skill` (any host: `--agent claude-code`, `copilot`, `cursor`, `codex`, `gemini`), or use the copy bundled in the wheel.

### `penult`

Take an idea (a GitHub issue) to a publication draft posted for the author’s review, then, once they approve, to an unpublished Substack or Medium draft. Use on “make a draft for <issue url>”, “turn this issue into an essay”, “write up issue N for Substack”, “draft the next essay”, “post the draft on the issue”, “they approved it, publish the draft”, or whenever an essay goes from a seed to a reviewed draft. Drives the whole path with the penult verbs (workspace, state, images within budget, issue comment, publishing hand-off) and the skills that own each step: do-research for checking claims and finding critiques, penlike (and its author-choice guide) and deslop for voice, ductus for machine-sounding passages, illustration for credited images. Posts the draft only where the author asked (the issue thread, public if the repository is); never publishes to a platform, and never sends anything to a platform before the author says the posted draft is good.

```bash
gh skill install thorwhalen/penult penult --agent claude-code
```

Source: [`penult/data/skills/penult`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/penult/tree/HEAD/penult/data/skills/penult) (bundled with the pip package).

The bundled skills are also on disk after `pip install penult`, under the package’s `data/skills/` directory; link them into an agent without network access with `skill link-skills <that directory>`.

## Instruction files

Files agents read before working in this repository.

- [`.claude/CLAUDE.md`](https://github.com/thorwhalen/penult/tree/HEAD/.claude/CLAUDE.md): read by Claude Code

## Machine-readable documentation

This site publishes the same documentation in forms that fit an agent’s context window:

- [`llms.txt`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/penult/llms.txt): an index of every page with a one-line description ([llms.txt](https://llmstxt.org) format)
- [`penult.md`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/penult/penult.md): the whole documentation as one Markdown file
- `<page>.html.md`: a rendered Markdown twin of every page, advertised from each page’s `<head>` with `<link rel="alternate" type="text/markdown">`
- [`objects.inv`](https://thorwhalen.github.io/penult/objects.inv): the Sphinx inventory: a symbol-to-URL index (`sphobjinv convert plain objects.inv -`)
